children: China and Hong Kong stocks inched higher on Wednesday as investors looked past the Trump administration's latest tariff proposal and joined a regional rally.
climbed as much as 0.5% in opening trade, bouncing from a 17-month low hit in the previous session. The Shanghai Composite Index
added 0.1%, also recovering from the lowest level since July 2025.
** Hong Kong shares were also upbeat, with the benchmark Hang Seng
up 1.6% to rebound from its lowest level since April 2025. The Hang Seng Tech Index

** US President Donald Trump proposed maximum potential tariffs of 20% to 40% on 14 major trading partners including China on Wednesday, in a move to counter excess industrial capacity that his administration has said these countries promote.
** A spokesperson for China's embassy in Washington rejected the assertion that China is a source of excess capacity.
** Around the region, Asian shares eked out gains after Wall Street fought back from deep lows, though the mood was muted in a holiday-thinned session.
** The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq retreated on Tuesday due to an AI selloff but finished well off the day's lows as bargain hunters stepped in.
